translations.answer: Fix Ubuntu, ROS Noetic, Python, and the target release version, explicitly load the Workspace Environment Sourcing, compile and run the Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP) or Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) example for OCS2; then add legged_controllers, Gazebo, and real machine hardware packages sequentially. Address missing dependencies for move_base_msgs, python3-catkin-tools, and empy, and use -DPYTHON_EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/python3 to fix the build interpreter. Avoid full recompilation repeatedly.
translations.applicability: Suitable for ROS Noetic + catkin-tools legged_control / OCS2 stack; command and package names must be verified against the current distribution.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Complete missing ros-noetic-navigation, python3-catkin-tools, or Python modules, and use -DPYTHON_EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/python3 to fix the build interpreter.
translations.details.attempts.1: Suggest using root to bypass sched_setscheduler permissions; this is a candidate for validation, not a recommended solution.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compile and run OCS2 DDP/SQP example first, then separately compile legged_controllers, Gazebo, and real machine hardware packages; explicitly source ROS and workspace environment in each terminal; retain the first error rather than just the final chain of errors.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Cross-reference the text, seven visible comments, and an image; community experience has not been independently verified by official documentation, source code, or issue.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The text provides corresponding commands for missing move_base_msgs, catkin-tools, and empy/Python interpreter; whether this applies to the current distribution requires verification.
translations.details.environments.0: Ubuntu + ROS Noetic; catkin-tools; OCS2, Pinocchio, hpp-fcl; Unitree A1 Gazebo simulation.
translations.details.limits.0: The article is intended for ROS Noetic and older dependency combinations; switching system Python directly or using root throughout may pollute the environment or expand permissions.
translations.details.limits.1: Comments cannot be linked individually; only the root post link and visible comments should be retained.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The text establishes a layered startup path from OCS2 example, controller, simulation, to real machine dependencies; real-time permissions and 'falling' issues in the robot are not fully closed-looped.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When compiling the first time for legged_control / OCS2, missing packages, Python modules, or catkin commands occur; how to locate issues by layer?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Controller startup fails with 'sched_setscheduler' permission; should it be run as root?
translations.details.problem_statements.2: The robot falls on the ground in simulation; does the post provide sufficient diagnostic information?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Prioritize verifying ulimit, group permissions, and minimal Linux capabilities when dealing with real-time scheduling; do not treat 'sudo su and run entire control stack' as a default practice.
translations.details.safety_notes.1: Limit the robot to simulation and lifting conditions before real deployment; set speed, force, and emergency stop, and record joint and contact logs.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Missing dependencies or Python modules; build toolchain pointing to the wrong Python interpreter; terminal not sourced; real-time scheduling capabilities or resource limits are insufficient.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The 'falling' motion in the robot lacks control mode, joint state, contact force, and logs; this cannot be reliably diagnosed at this stage.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Missing move_base_msgs, rospkg, defusedxml, empy, or catkin; no permission to call real-time scheduling interface; robot falls on the ground.
translations.media_summaries.0: The text contains the only engineering diagram for showing optional gait/control mode; refer to the configuration in load_controller.launch and rqt instructions for full understanding; the image does not provide joint, contact force, or optimizer logs, so it cannot explain the 'falling' symptom in the comment.
